summary.title: Power Up Your Team with Nonviolent Communication Principles
summary.one_liner: You learn the nonviolent communication framework (observation, emotional audit, needs, requests) and the A-E-I-O-U conflict model that executive coaches Ann Mehl and Jerry Colonna use with startup teams.
keywords: how to communicate clearly at work
takeaways: Separate observations from judgments: state what you see and hear, not what you conclude about it.
Use the four NVC ingredients: observation, emotional audit, needs, and requests phrased with flexibility.
Handle conflict with the A-E-I-O-U model (Acknowledge, Express, Identify, Outcome, Understanding), assuming both sides mean well.
Model the behavior yourself first, ask people to repeat instructions back, and expect multiple rounds to resolve conflicts.
Reset tense conversations by pausing, or by recalling the team's shared history and mission.
summary.summary: This First Round Review article interviews executive coaches Ann Mehl and Jerry Colonna about nonviolent communication (NVC), a method built on awareness, responsibility and empathy. It explains the four NVC ingredients (observation, emotional audit, needs, requests) with examples, and contrasts open and closed questions. It then walks through Mehl's A-E-I-O-U model for managing workplace conflict, with practical steps for founders, moderators and teams. The closing sections cover how to introduce these habits to a team and why better communication helps productivity.
